question: An agentic workflow sends requests with a large tools array (15 tool definitions, cached), a cached system prompt, and growing conversation history. For one request, the developer adds tool_choice: {"type": "tool", "name": "search"} to force a specific tool call, while leaving the tools array, system prompt, and message content unchanged. What happens to prompt caching for this request?
options: A) Nothing is invalidated, because tool_choice is a request-level parameter that sits outside the cached tools, system, and messages hierarchy entirely.
B) Only the tools-array cache is invalidated, but the system prompt and message cache remain valid since tool_choice only affects which tool definitions are considered.
C) The entire cache is invalidated because tool_choice changes are treated the same as editing the tools array itself, forcing a full recomputation from the first block.
D) Only the message-level cache is invalidated, so tokens up through the system prompt are still served from cache while the messages must be reprocessed.
correct_answers: D) Only the message-level cache is invalidated, so tokens up through the system prompt are still served from cache while the messages must be reprocessed.
explanations: Incorrect. tool_choice does affect caching: it is one of the request properties whose change invalidates the message-level cache, so it is not entirely outside the hierarchy.
Incorrect. tool_choice does not invalidate the tools-array cache; the tool definitions are unchanged. It invalidates the message-level cache instead, while the tools and system caches stay valid.
Incorrect. Changing tool_choice is not equivalent to editing the tool definitions themselves; it only affects the message-level cache, not the tools-array cache.

Correct. Cache invalidation cascades downward through tools, then system, then messages. A tool_choice change only invalidates the message-level cache; the tools and system caches, which sit above it in the hierarchy, remain valid and are still served from cache.
